claims.text: Role in hypercalcemia: bisphos inhibit osteoclasts - USU drugs of choice for CA-assoc hypercalcemia;
claims.quote: Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclasts. They are usually the medications of choice for cancer-associated hypercalcemia.

claims.text: zoledronic acid 4 mg IV once ↓Ca avg > 40 days;
claims.quote: Zoledronic acid can be given as a one-time dose of 4 mg IV and lowers serum calcium very effectively for an average of > 40 days.

claims.text: pamidronate 60 to 90 mg IV once - repeat only after 7 days - ↓Ca ≤ 2 wks;
claims.quote: Pamidronate can be given for cancer-associated hypercalcemia as a one-time dose of 60 to 90 mg IV, repeated only after 7 days. It lowers serum calcium for ≤ 2 weeks.

claims.text: repeated IV bisphos (bone mets · myeloma) → ONJ - renal toxicity w zoledronic acid;
claims.quote: Repetitive use of IV bisphosphonates to treat hypercalcemia associated with metastatic bone disease or myeloma has been associated with osteonecrosis of the jaw. Some reports suggest this finding may be more common with zoledronic acid. Renal toxicity has been reported in patients receiving zoledronic acid.

claims.text: PO bisphos maintain norm Ca but ⍉generally used acutely;
claims.quote: Oral bisphosphonates (eg, alendronate or risedronate) can be given to maintain calcium in the normal range but are not generally used for treating hypercalcemia acutely.

claims.text: denosumab: CA-assoc hypercalcemia ⍉responding to bisphos - 120 mg SC Q4wks + extra doses days 8 & 15 of first mo;
claims.quote: Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody inhibitor of osteoclastic activity that can be used for cancer-associated hypercalcemia that does not respond to bisphosphonates. Dosage is 120 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks with additional doses on days 8 and 15 of the first month of treatment.

claims.text: give Ca & vitD prn to avert hypocalcemia;
claims.quote: Calcium and vitamin D are given as needed to avert hypocalcemia.

claims.text: calcitonin (salmon) 4 to 8 IU/kg SC every 12 h - ↓Ca 1 to 2 mg/dL w.in few hrs;
claims.quote: A salmon calcitonin dosage of 4 to 8 IU/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours is safe. Calcitonin can lower serum calcium levels by 1 to 2 mg/dL within a few hours.

claims.text: in CA-assoc hypercalcemia, limited by short action w tachyphylaxis (often after ~48 h) & ⍉response in ≥ 40%.
claims.quote: Its usefulness in the treatment of cancer-associated hypercalcemia is limited by its short duration of action with the development of tachyphylaxis (often after about 48 hours) and by the lack of response in ≥ 40% of patients.

claims.text: salmon calcitonin + prednisone may control Ca for mo in some CA pts
claims.quote: the combination of salmon calcitonin and prednisone may control serum calcium for several months in some patients with cancer

claims.text: Denosumab (Xgeva) safety: CI: hypocalcemia (must be corrected b4 starting Xgeva).
claims.quote: Pre-existing hypocalcemia must be corrected prior to initiating therapy with Xgeva

claims.text: CI: known clinically sig hypersensitivity to Xgeva or denosumab prod.
claims.quote: Known clinically significant hypersensitivity to Xgeva or denosumab products

claims.text: Can cause severe Sxtomatic hypocalcemia w fatal cases - correct hypocalcemia b4 starting - monitor Ca esp first wks - adequately supp all pts w Ca & vitD.
claims.quote: Xgeva can cause severe symptomatic hypocalcemia, and fatal cases have been reported. Correct hypocalcemia prior to initiating Xgeva. Monitor calcium levels during therapy, especially in the first weeks of initiating therapy, and adequately supplement all patients with calcium and vitamin D.

claims.text: ↑ risk of hypocalcemia w increasing renal dysfun, MC severe dysfun (CrCl < 30 mL/min and/or on dialysis), & w inadeq/⍉Ca supp.
claims.quote: An increased risk of hypocalcemia has been observed in clinical trials of patients with increasing renal dysfunction, most commonly with severe dysfunction (creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min and/or on dialysis), and with inadequate/no calcium supplementation.

claims.text: Hypersensitivity rxns incl anaphylaxis may occur - d/c permanently if clinically sig rxn occurs.
claims.quote: Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis may occur. Discontinue permanently if a clinically significant reaction occurs.

claims.text: ONJ reported - oral exam b4 starting - monitor for Sx - ⍉ invasive dental procedures during tx.
claims.quote: Osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) has been reported in patients receiving Xgeva. Perform an oral examination prior to starting Xgeva. Monitor for symptoms. Avoid invasive dental procedures during treatment with Xgeva.

claims.text: Atypical femoral frx: evaluate pts w thigh or groin pain to r/o femoral frx.
claims.quote: Atypical femoral fracture: Evaluate patients with thigh or groin pain to rule out a femoral fracture.
claims.locator: 5.5 Atypical Subtrochanteric and Diaphyseal Femoral Fracture

claims.text: Multi vertebral frx reported after discontinuation - when Xgeva = stopped, evaluate the pt's risk for vertebral frx.
claims.quote: When Xgeva treatment is discontinued, evaluate the individual patient’s risk for vertebral fractures
claims.locator: 5.7 Multiple Vertebral Fractures (MVF) Following Treatment Discontinuation

claims.text: Hypercalcemia requiring hsp & complicated by acute renal inj reported after tx discontinuation in pts w giant cell tumor of bone & growing skeletons.
claims.quote: Clinically significant hypercalcemia requiring hospitalization and complicated by acute renal injury has been reported in Xgeva-treated patients with giant cell tumor of bone and patients with growing skeletons.
claims.locator: 5.6 Hypercalcemia Following Treatment Discontinuation in Patients with Giant Cell Tumor of Bone and in Patients with Growing Skeletons

claims.text: May cause fetal harm - advise females of reprod potential to use effective contraception during therapy & for ≥ 5 mo after the last dose.
claims.quote: Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during therapy, and for at least 5 months after the last dose of Xgeva

claims.text: Pts receiving Xgeva should ⍉ receive other denosumab prod concomitantly
claims.quote: Patients receiving Xgeva should not receive other denosumab products concomitantly.
claims.locator: 5.1 Drug Products with Same Active Ingredient

claims.text: Calcitonin salmon (Miacalcin) safety: CI: hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any excipients (rxns incl anaphylaxis w death, bronchospasm, & swelling of the tongue or throat).
claims.quote: Hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients. Reactions have included anaphylaxis with death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat

claims.text: Serious hypersensitivity rxns incl fatal anaphylaxis reported - consider skin testing b4 tx in pts w sus hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon.
claims.quote: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including reports of fatal anaphylaxis have been reported. Consider skin testing prior to treatment in patients with suspected hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon

claims.text: Hypocalcemia w tetany (musc cramps · twitching) & sz activity reported - hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy.
claims.quote: Hypocalcemia associated with tetany (i.e., muscle cramps, twitching) and seizure activity has been reported with Miacalcin injection therapy. Hypocalcemia must be corrected before initiating therapy.

claims.text: Meta-analysis of 21 trials suggests ↑ risk of overall malig in calcitonin salmon-treated pts.
claims.quote: A meta-analysis of 21 clinical trials suggests an increased risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated patients

claims.text: Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop & may cause loss of response to tx.
claims.quote: Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop, and may cause loss of response to treatment

claims.text: Use for Paget's dz or postmenopausal osteoporosis = recommended w adequate intake of Ca & vitD.
claims.quote: Use of Miacalcin injection for the treatment of Paget’s disease or postmenopausal osteoporosis is recommended in conjunction with an adequate intake of calcium and vitamin D

claims.text: Concomitant lithium may ↓ plasma lithium concentrations (↑ urinary clearance) - lithium dose may require adj.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of calcitonin salmon and lithium may lead to a reduction in plasma lithium concentrations due to increased urinary clearance of lithium. The dose of lithium may require adjustment.

claims.text: OD: hypocalcemic tetany could occur - keep parenteral calcium available for tx.
claims.quote: The pharmacologic actions of Miacalcin injection suggest that hypocalcemic tetany could occur in overdose. Therefore, provisions for parenteral administration of calcium should be available for the treatment of overdose.

claims.text: MC adverse rxns: nausea w or w.o vomiting (10%) · inj site inflam (10%) & flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%).
claims.quote: Most common adverse reactions are nausea with or without vomiting (10%), injection site inflammation (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%)

claims.text: ←the poss assoc b/n malig & calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated periodically
claims.quote: Due to the possible association between malignancy and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated on a periodic basis
